questions.problem: Write the following series in sigma notation: $-5+25-125+625-⋯.$
questions.worked_solution:
The first term is ${a}_{1}=-5$ and the second term is ${a}_{2}=25.$ Using these two terms, we compute the common ratio:

$$
r=\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}}=\frac{25}{-5}=-5
$$

Therefore, the general term can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}{(r)}^{n-1} \\  & =-5{(-5)}^{n-1} \\  & =-5{(-5)}^{-1}{(-5)}^{n} \\  & =-5(-\frac{1}{5}){(-5)}^{n} \\  & ={(-5)}^{n}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the infinite geometric series can be written in sigma notation as

$$
\begin{aligned}-5+25-125+625-⋯ & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{(-5)}^{n}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Write the following series in sigma notation: $40+20+10+5+….$
questions.worked_solution:
The first term is ${a}_{1}=40$ and the second term is ${a}_{2}=20.$ Using these two terms, we compute the common ratio:

$$
r=\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}}=\frac{20}{40}=\frac{1}{2}
$$

Therefore, the general term can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}{(r)}^{n-1} \\  & =40{(\frac{1}{2})}^{n-1} \\  & =40{(\frac{1}{2})}^{-1}{(\frac{1}{2})}^{n} \\  & =40(\frac{2}{1}){(\frac{1}{2})}^{n} \\  & =80{(\frac{1}{2})}^{n}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the infinite geometric series can be written in sigma notation as

$$
\begin{aligned}40+20+10+5+⋯ & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }80{(\frac{1}{2})}^{n}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Consider the infinite geometric series starting from ${a}_{1}=-14$  with the property $\frac{{a}_{n+1}}{{a}_{n}}=-\frac{1}{7}.$ Write the sum to infinity of the terms of this series using sigma notation.
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that the sequence is a geometric sequence since the ratio of any two successive terms is constant.

The first term of the sequence is ${a}_{1}=-14,$ and the common ratio is

$$
r=\frac{{a}_{n+1}}{{a}_{n}}=-\frac{1}{7}.
$$

Therefore, the general term ${a}_{n}$ can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}{(r)}^{n-1} \\  & =-14{(-\frac{1}{7})}^{n-1} \\  & =-14{(-\frac{1}{7})}^{-1}{(-\frac{1}{7})}^{n} \\  & =98{(-\frac{1}{7})}^{n}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the infinite geometric series can be written in sigma notation as

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n} & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }98{(-\frac{1}{7})}^{n}.\end{aligned}
$$
